title: Refactor Motoko resolve-or-create school helper (internal only) and clean up backend call sites

requirements.text: Refactor the internal Motoko implementation of the existing private school helper(s) so the resolve-or-create-by-exact-school-name behavior remains identical, but the code is simplified and deduplicated (including factoring repeated checks, reducing nested switches, and improving readability).

quotes: to modify only the internal Motoko implementation of the resolve-or-create helper, without changing its external behavior

acceptanceCriteria: No public/shared method signatures change as part of this refactor.
The helper still performs exact Text equality lookup against the existing exactSchoolNameRegistry and creates a new School record when missing.
Authorization semantics remain unchanged (only teachers/admins can resolve/create schools).
Project builds successfully after refactor (Motoko compilation succeeds).

requirements.text: Refactor manager-assignment logic used by school auto-creation to improve code quality without changing behavior, ensuring the same persisted effects on userProfiles and the same trapping behavior for invalid school IDs.
acceptanceCriteria: When a school is auto-created through the helper, the caller is still assigned as that school's manager exactly as before.
If manager assignment is attempted for a non-existent school ID, the behavior remains a trap (no silent failures).
No user-facing text changes are introduced as part of this refactor.

requirements.text: Clean up backend entry points that accept a school name (Text) to call the shared resolve-or-create helper consistently, removing duplicate resolve/create/authorization logic at call sites while keeping outcomes identical.

quotes: changes apply inside the helper, and also refactor how other backend entry points call it

acceptanceCriteria: All backend flows that accept a school name (Text) delegate school ID resolution/creation to the single shared helper (no duplicated resolution logic remains at call sites).
No call-site refactor changes the externally observed behavior (returned values and trap conditions remain the same for equivalent inputs).
Project builds successfully after call-site refactors (Motoko compilation succeeds).

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor; do not introduce additional canisters/services.
Do not change external behavior of the resolve-or-create school helper or the backend entry points that depend on it (refactor/code-quality only).
Do not introduce fuzzy/normalized/partial matching; exact Text equality semantics must remain unchanged.
Use English for any user-facing text.
nonGoals: Frontend/UI changes (this task is backend-only refactoring).
Adding new product features (e.g., new school/class workflows beyond existing behavior).
Changing data schemas or requiring state migration unless strictly necessary for the refactor.
